headline: Red Wings place Jacob Bernard-Docker on waivers
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Red Wings have placed Jacob Bernard-Docker on waivers, noting he has missed the start of the season with an upper-body injury. That is all the report gives us, so there is no word yet on whether another team will claim him.

The more interesting question is what it means for a Detroit team that sits at 2-3-2 with six points through seven games. The record undersells how they have played. DET has driven 51.1 percent of the expected goals so far this season, and 53 percent at five-on-five, so the chances have tilted their way more often than not. The problem is finishing: Detroit is 7.4 goals below expected, the kind of gap that usually reflects shooting luck more than a broken process. Their goaltending, at 2.4 goals saved above expected, has been fine. The special teams are quiet, with the power play generating 0.92 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.76. Since Bernard-Docker has not played, his absence cannot explain any of this, and losing him changes little for a team whose underlying numbers are already decent.
